dropped_from_p3.reason: Qualified and dropped on the three-survivor cap (owner, 2026-09-28), not on a value. P3's finding holds: P2's reasons, price and an OE pin wired low, are not requirement values. It passes: 40 lines in 1 part (33 needed, 7 spare); RESET active low, power-up default every I/O an input, no internal pull-ups on the I/Os, internal pull-ups on none of AD2:AD0; Fm+ to 1 MHz; VDD 2.3 to 5.5 V; Tamb -40 to +85 degC; 64 addresses, of which 7-bit 0x20 (AD2:AD0 = VSS, VSS, VSS) is clear of every listed address (PCA9698 Rev. 3, 3 August 2010, 7.1, 7.9, Table 12, https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/data-sheet/PCA9698.pdf, vendors.py fetch HTTP 200, 2026-10-02T14:35:00Z). JLCPCB C729177 stockCount 1908, canPresaleNumber 1894, expand, USD 8.4469 at 10 (14:36:39Z) against 50 for 5 placements; Digi-Key stock_available 3322, lead 16 weeks, Active (14:27:10Z cached). It ranks fourth among 4 qualified parts: USD 8.45 against about 2.7 for two TCA6424ARGJR, 7 spare lines against 15, and one part carrying all 33 lines in a TSSOP56. Its OE input 3-states every output, which no other option has; it is a wiring choice, not a requirement.

P3's finding does not change the drop. The requirement is 'Latch until action' (V130, V280), and the Follow-ups row of Research.md puts the latch into this function ('each failed the +/-0.99 % HV trip band or the latch'). TPS3701 has no latch: OUTB goes high again when the sense voltage falls below VIT-(INB); the word latch does not occur in SBVS240C (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps3701.pdf, vendors.py fetch HTTP 200, 2026-10-02T14:39:04Z). It meets both trip bands (VIT+(INB) 397 to 403 mV, +/-0.75 %, so 8.533 to 8.697 V with 0.1 % resistors) and rule 4 (JLCPCB C132788 26813 / 26784, 14:37:53Z). R3 holds its latch (74LVC1G175GW,125, F11) as its own function; R6 has no latch function in Follow-ups or selection.json. A latch function for the 20 ports is a gap for a P1 follow-up, and TPS3701DDCR is the comparator it would pair with. Reported, not ranked.

Same as TPS3701DDCR: no latch (the word does not occur in SNVSAV4B, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tlv6710.pdf, 2026-10-02T14:39:05Z); INB band VIT+(INB) 397 to 403 mV and rule 4 pass (JLCPCB C2863066 3103 / 3091, 14:37:54Z).

P3 is right that P2's reason (0.9 % to 2.5 %) does not hold for the falling threshold, but the part still fails, on three values. (1) HV trip band: the overvoltage trip is the rising threshold VIT+, 400 to 413 mV (+/-1.6 % about 406.5 mV, before any divider), over +/-0.99 %; the 0.75 % applies to VIT- 397 to 403 mV only (SBVS331B 7.5, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tlv6713.pdf, vendors.py fetch HTTP 200, 2026-10-02T14:38:00Z). TLV6710 and TPS3701 reach +/-0.75 % on the rising edge only through INB, the inverting input, which TLV6713 does not have. (2) Rule 4: JLCPCB C2861351 stockCount 167 under 500 (need 100, S4), C2872139 0 (14:37:50Z). (3) Latch until action: none.
